{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Robert Scott Rumely''' (born 1952) is a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Georgia]] who specializes in [[number theory]] and [[arithmetic geometry]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.math.uga.edu/directory/robert-rumely|title=Robert Rumely|work=Mathematics Department Directory|publisher=University of Georgia|accessdate=2015-11-17}}.</ref> He is one of the inventors of the [[Adleman–Pomerance–Rumely primality test]].<ref>{{citation|title=Secret History: The Story of Cryptology|series=Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications|first=Craig P.|last=Bauer|publisher=CRC Press|year=2013|isbn=9781466561861|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EBkEGAOlCDsC&pg=PA468|page=468}}.</ref>

==Life==
Rumely was born on June 23, 1952, in [[Pullman, Washington]]. He graduated from [[Grinnell College]] in 1974,<ref name="cv">{{citation|url=http://alpha.math.uga.edu/~rr/RumelyResProfVita2012.pdf|title=Curriculum vitae: Robert Scott Rumely|accessdate=2015-11-17}}.</ref> and completed his Ph.D. in 1978 at [[Princeton University]] under the supervision of [[Goro Shimura]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=80059}}</ref> After temporary positions at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] and [[Harvard University]], he joined the University of Georgia faculty in 1981.<ref name="cv"/>

Rumely has taught a summer [[Research Experiences for Undergraduates]] program on the [[mathematics of paper folding]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://onlineathens.com/stories/072609/uga_470969696.shtml|title=Math professor brings students into the fold with origami|date=July 26, 2009|first=Lee|last=Shearer|newspaper=[[Athens Banner-Herald]]}}.</ref>

==Books==
He is the author or co-author of four books:
*''Capacity Theory on Algebraic Curves'' (''[[Lecture Notes in Mathematics]]'' 1378, 1989)<ref>Review of ''Capacity Theory on Algebraic Curves'' by Daniel Barsky (1991), {{MR|1009368}}</ref><ref>{{citation
 | last = Chinburg | first = Ted
 | doi = 10.1090/S0273-0979-1992-00262-8
 | issue = 2
 | journal = [[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]]
 | mr = 1567972
 | pages = 332–336
 | series = New Series
 | title = Book Review: Capacity theory on algebraic curves
 | volume = 26
 | year = 1992| doi-access = free
 }}</ref>
*''Existence of the Sectional Capacity'' (''[[Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society]]'' 145, 2000)<ref>Review of ''Existence of the Sectional Capacity'' by Klaus Künnemann (2000), ''[[Mathematical Reviews]]'' Featured Review, {{MR|1677934}}</ref>
*''Potential Theory and Dynamics on the Berkovich Projective Line'' (''[[Mathematical Surveys and Monographs]]'' 159, 2010)<ref>Review of ''Potential Theory and Dynamics on the Berkovich Projective Line'' by Charles Favre (2012), {{MR|2599526}}</ref>
*''Capacity Theory with Local Rationality: The Strong Fekete-Szegö Theorem on Curves'' (''[[Mathematical Surveys and Monographs]]'' 193, 2013)<ref>Review of ''Capacity Theory with Local Rationality'' by Laura G. DeMarco, {{MR|3154724}}</ref>

==Awards==
In 2015 he was elected as a [[American Mathematical Society#Fellows|Fellow of the American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to arithmetic potential theory, computational number theory, and arithmetic dynamics".<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/profession/ams-fellows/new-fellows|title=2016 Class of the Fellows of the AMS|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|accessdate=2015-11-17}}.</ref>
